content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm [user_name] and this is my first post on this forum. I'm working on a project to control both lighting and climate at my workplace. The design currently uses 17 [product_name] modules (software version [version_no]); 5 are set up for heating management, while the other 12 handle lighting, window operation, and temperature readings for climate control. Since control is via an HMI panel programmed in [product_name] with [version_no], which allows up to 16 connections, I've centralized some module connections and redistributed commands through networked inputs/outputs. However, after adding the latest [product_name] module, connection lines in the network view switched from solid to dashed. The software shows no errors (there were errors previously when exceeding connection limits), and after checking both documentation and online resources, I couldn't find an explanation for dashed versus continuous lines. Could someone clarify the function or meaning of this? Any feedback on the project setup would also be welcome. I've attached a network view screenshot; device lines are hidden for clarity. Thanks in advance!

This visual effect appears if S7 access is not enabled in a [product_name] ([version_no]). Without S7 access, the module cannot communicate with other devices over Ethernet TCP/IP using the S7 protocol. [IMAGE]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering unexpected dashed lines in the network view when connecting several [product_name] modules in [product_name] software ([version_no]). There's confusion about the significance of these dashed connections, since no error or warning is triggered by the software, leading to uncertainty for those building larger controller networks and integrating HMI panels.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear visual cues and documentation on network connection statuses and limitations, so they can reliably plan complex, multi-device networks with confidence.
